name: Coordinated termination-risk response and evidence preservation

attribution.legal_posture: Sophos and DTEX defensive response guidance is informed by reported risk; guidance describes reported risk and leaves individual worker conduct case-specific.

caveats: Apply controls consistently with privacy, employment, labor, accessibility, retention, notice, correction, and access-governance requirements.
Counsel-approved communications and established incident-response/law-enforcement channels are the appropriate route; retaliatory or deceptive engagement is outside the process.
Pre-termination downloads, handoffs, forwarding, and severance questions can be legitimate business activity.
Preserve evidence proportionately and respect employment, monitoring, privacy, and labor law.
Use the pattern to prioritize documented human-led review; DPRK affiliation, fraud, and malicious intent require a combined evidence record.

statements: Before an adverse termination, inventory sessions, tokens, repositories, secrets, data stores, forwarding rules, integrations, and managed devices; revoke in a coordinated window.
Preserve logs and legal hold material, monitor unusual pre-termination downloads and post-revocation access attempts, and establish a controlled channel for extortion communications.
Separate evidence preservation and employee safety from attribution: respond to the behavior even when DPRK linkage is uncertain.
limitations: Pre-termination downloads, handoffs, forwarding, and severance questions can be legitimate business activity.
Do not conduct retaliatory or deceptive engagement; use counsel-approved communications and established incident-response/law-enforcement channels.
Preserve evidence proportionately and respect employment, monitoring, privacy, and labor law.
